title: Database Developer Roadmap
description: A curated, stage-by-stage path from SQL fundamentals to advanced querying, database design, PostgreSQL, and SQL interview preparation.
audience: Beginners learning databases for the first time, and developers who use ORMs but have never learned SQL properly.
intro: Databases reward depth: a small number of concepts — set-based thinking, normalization, indexing — explain most performance and design questions. Learn them once, properly.

stages.title: SQL Foundations
stages.description: Start with the language of databases: SELECT, filtering, sorting, aggregates, and joins. Everything else in this roadmap builds on these statements.
stages.milestone: You can answer business questions about a sample database using joins, GROUP BY, and subqueries without looking up syntax.

steps.note: Work through the fundamentals modules first; the syntax transfers almost entirely to other databases.
Your revision sheet once the basics are done.

stages.title: Hands-On Practice
stages.description: SQL is a skill, not a topic. Solve progressively harder problems until writing queries feels automatic.
stages.milestone: You can solve medium-difficulty query problems under time pressure, using window functions when they simplify the query.

steps.note: Do at least the beginner and intermediate modules; revisit failed problems after a day.

stages.title: Database Design
stages.description: Writing queries is half the job. Schema design — tables, keys, relationships, normalization — determines how well the system ages.
stages.milestone: You can turn a vague requirement into a normalized schema with clear relationships, and defend each design decision.

steps.note: Design each schema on paper (or in a diagram tool) before reading the solution.

stages.title: PostgreSQL
stages.description: PostgreSQL is the most requested open-source database in job listings. Learn how it differs from SQL Server and what its tooling offers.
stages.milestone: You can install PostgreSQL, model data in it, write advanced queries, and use its data types and indexing options appropriately.

steps.note: Pay attention to the differences from SQL Server — knowing both makes you adaptable.

stages.title: Interview Preparation
stages.description: Consolidate with a question bank that mirrors real database interviews: syntax, design trade-offs, and performance reasoning.
stages.milestone: You can write correct SQL on a whiteboard or shared editor and explain query performance choices, not just produce working queries.
